paragraphs: Here's Zophar's big idea: "the triumph of the wicked has been brief" (Job 20:5). One part of his speech is worth keeping. He says the man loses it all because "he has oppressed and forsaken the poor" (Job 20:19), and that his appetite is never satisfied (Job 20:20). Friend, grabbing from people who have little never fills you up, and it matters to God. So check your own hands before you go checking anybody else's.

But a speech can be LOUD and still not be the whole picture. Zophar says his anxious thoughts push him to answer (Job 20:2), and he does not come in gently. I once told my whole bakery with total confidence that the oven was off. The oven disagreed. I think sounding sure and being right are two different things, so a baker keeps listening.

Why does that matter? Job had just said, "But I know that my Redeemer lives…" (Job 19:25), and Zophar answers with a tidy rule about how things go for the wicked. I think a tidy rule can sound wise and still have no room for someone who is hurting. So hold on to what's true in it, keep your ears open for the rest, and remember this conversation is FAR from over.
